findings.diagnosis: The prompt underestimates how destructive a following predicate/qualification can be: cuts that leave a preverbal fragment, an incomplete predicate, or an existential/qualification (e.g. 'may be the presence ...') are often contradicted or made misleading by what follows and must be ranked far lower.
findings.evidence: 10 cases (en_us_1591, en_us_1593, en_us_1102, en_us_1192, en_us_1427, en_us_1143, en_us_1108, en_us_608, en_us_594, en_us_388) where a single policy-kept cut had very high measured contra (>0.8) and that one cut alone zeroed or collapsed the set; in each the kept cut left a fragment that only gains its truth or qualification from later material (preverbal fragments, existential 'may be ...', or list disambiguation).

edit.text: 1) Contra: Could the remainder of the sentence overturn or contradict the stretch already spoken?  Treat this quantitatively and aggressively: compute target = cohesion * (1 - contra) and use that product to order cuts. Any candidate with contra >= 0.6 will make (1 - contra) <= 0.4 and thus should be given a substantially lower score than typical low‑contra candidates; in practice rank all high‑contra (>=0.6) positions below low‑contra positions so the downstream step does not keep them. Do not rely on intuition alone — estimate contra as a probability and let the (1 - contra) multiplier decisively push cuts that leave incomplete predicates or existential/qualification fragments toward the bottom of the ordering.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt downplays cohesion loss from splitting multiword units: breaking titles/names, a noun/verb head from its essential modifiers or objects, list items or quantifier frames frequently destroys translatability and should be penalised strongly.
findings.evidence: 9 cases (en_us_1591, en_us_388, en_us_594, en_us_1108, en_us_1102, en_us_1143, en_us_1427, en_us_608, en_us_1192) where the policy cut inside named titles, noun phrases, verb+object frames or list/coordinate structures and kept those cuts despite high cohesion loss; the offline targets preserve such multiword units and score much higher.

Output: may be the presence <SEG:5> of an open container <SEG:95>
(Explanation: cutting after 'presence' separates the existential predicate from its object; cohesion drops sharply and the cut must receive a very low score so it is not selected under realistic latency budgets.)
